Rhyme of Way,
ranked by rhyme.

Riley Walz mapped every U.S. intersection where the street names rhyme — walzr.com/rhyme-of-way. His list is already filtered to rhymes. This page reranks the same 5,482 pairs by how much they rhyme: double and mosaic locks rise; template dumps like Hill & Mill sink.

Source: intersection list and coordinates from Rhyme of Way by Riley Walz (intersections.json, snapshot 2026-09-05). Scoring and this page by How To Move The Needle. Not affiliated with Walz.
How the score works

Each pair is scored on the stripped names already in Walz’s data (na / nb — no Street/Avenue/Road).

  • Rhyme tail from the CMU Pronouncing Dictionary: last primary-stressed vowel through the end of the word.
  • Type: Triple / Double (extra rhyming syllables) beat a one-syllable Perfect. Phrase = two-word names whose last words lock. Mosaic = two or more aligned content words rhyme (Old Dairy & Gold Berry).
  • Penalties for overused families (Hill/Mill, Fourth/North, Creek/Peak), identical stems, and tiny common pairs (Bay/Way).

This is rhyme strength, not Walz’s browse/discovery ranking. A 18 on Hill & Mill still rhymes. It just rhymes the same way 800 other corners do.
